profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal troubleshooting meeting at a Jakarta law firm representing a sharia insurance company after a policyholder filed a profit-sharing dispute over a mudarabah musytarakah life policy. The immediate problem is that the company's claims and legal teams are giving inconsistent guidance on where the dispute should be handled and what contractual document controls. The meeting is between the litigation lead and the regulatory counsel to diagnose why the internal response memo is inconsistent, identify the root cause of the forum-confusion problem, and agree on a corrective recommendation for the client before a response deadline. The agenda is to review the policy documents and endorsement history, compare them against Indonesian sharia insurance regulations and dispute-resolution practice, determine whether the clause set is internally coherent, and decide what 'fix' should be recommended. The expected outcome is a joint action plan for a revised legal memo and client advice on the proper dispute pathway and document remediation.

members.name: Alya Pranata
members.expertise: Insurance disputes, arbitration strategy, religious court procedure, contractual enforcement
members.background: Alya has spent seven years handling insurance and commercial disputes in Indonesian courts and arbitral forums, with recent matters involving sharia-compliant financial products and enforcement of dispute-resolution clauses.
members.private_state: Alya wants a clean, defensible position the client can use immediately if the policyholder escalates this week, and is concerned that any recommendation that weakens clause enforceability will reduce the client's leverage in settlement.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing the 'forum clause,' the operative text is the dispute-resolution clause inside the issued policy booklet and any rider physically delivered to the policyholder, because that is what will matter in a filed case.
A 'resolved' troubleshooting outcome means the company can point to one enforceable path for this live dispute without reopening product architecture across all legacy policies.
References to 'BASYARNAS first' in internal summaries naturally mean a binding adjudicative step under the contract, not merely a mediation-oriented or optional pre-litigation channel.
If an endorsement was approved internally but not clearly incorporated into the insured's policy package, it is not part of the practical litigation record for this dispute.

members.name: Rizki Maulana
members.expertise: Insurance regulation, OJK compliance, DSN-MUI sharia governance, product documentation
members.background: Rizki has worked in-house and in private practice advising insurers on product approvals, sharia governance structures, and alignment between policy wording, standard operating procedures, and Indonesian financial-services regulation.
members.private_state: Rizki wants to prevent the client from treating this as a one-off litigation issue when he suspects the real problem is a documentation-governance gap that could affect multiple products and trigger regulator scrutiny.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing the 'forum clause,' the relevant framework includes the policy, product filing package, standard dispute-handling SOP, and sharia governance materials that were approved as part of compliance operations.

A 'resolved' troubleshooting outcome means the documentation stack and escalation pathway are made compliant and internally consistent going forward, even if the present dispute still needs interim handling.

References to 'BASYARNAS first' naturally mean the standard sharia dispute-handling sequence recognized in practice, which may include consultation or mediated settlement before any formal adjudication.

If an endorsement or revised clause was included in the product governance and servicing system used by the insurer, it is operationally part of the contract framework unless expressly rejected, even if delivery evidence is imperfect.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the controlling forum clause
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss 'the forum clause' and 'the contract documents' as if referring to the same body of material.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the issued policy wording, signed application, and any rider or endorsement demonstrably delivered to the policyholder in this specific file.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the broader contract-and-compliance package, including product filing language, servicing SOPs, sharia governance documents, and system-applied endorsements used in administration.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal practice both speakers routinely compress multiple layers of documentation into shorthand like 'the clause' or 'the contract set,' so the shared terminology creates a natural illusion of alignment.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of 'resolved' for the troubleshooting task
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they need to 'fix the inconsistency' and 'resolve the issue today.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the issue is fixed once they can recommend one defensible forum position for the current policyholder dispute and explain away conflicting language.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the issue is fixed only if they identify and remediate the underlying documentation/process mismatch so the client's dispute pathway is compliant across similar policies.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Troubleshooting meetings often use broad action words like 'fix' and 'resolve' without spelling out completion criteria, especially when both immediate triage and systemic repair seem obviously desirable.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the file appears to require 'BASYARNAS first' before going elsewhere.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes this to mean the contract channels the dispute into BASYARNAS as the binding first adjudicative forum before any court involvement.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes this to mean BASYARNAS is the first step in the sharia dispute-resolution sequence in practice, potentially as a settlement-oriented stage before formal adjudication if needed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds professionally standard and both are familiar with BASYARNAS, so neither pauses to unpack whether they mean a binding forum designation, a staged escalation path, or a practice norm.

misalignment_points.topic: Which endorsement history they are referencing
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the 2021 endorsement' as the document that cleaned up the dispute language.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the April 2021 rider attached to several policy files that replaced the clause with a Religious Court fallback after deliberation failure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the September 2021 product-wide wording update submitted in the insurer's governance file that inserted BASYARNAS language into the standard template.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents were issued in 2021, both concerned dispute-resolution wording, and in internal discussions staff commonly collapse version history into a single shorthand year-reference.
